messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary rollout 'v5.3-canary' increased p99 latency on /v1/generate by 3.8x vs baseline. Auto-page oncall. metric-links: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/abcd123/canary-latency
Alex R: acked. I'm oncall. grabbing traces + heap of canary tasks.
Maya S: seeing spikes too — p95 up from 120ms -> 450ms, p99 up to 2.8s. Streaming stalls observed (clients report partial chunks).
Jordan T: logs show a burst of KV cache misses for canary shards around 1947654280. Could be a change in cache key prefixing in v5.3.
Samir K: confirmed config diff: v5.3 toggled 'kv_prefix_harmonize=true' -> that changes primary key structure. Might cause high cold cache thrash on new prefix.
Lia P: customer-impact: 3 customers reported timeouts from webhooks; CS-ops notified customers of degraded service. Not yet P1 but trending.
Alex R: initial mitigation options: 1) roll canary back to v5.2 2) throttle canary traffic to 5% 3) route streaming clients to stable model variant 4) scale canary pool + prewarm cache.
Maya S: can we quickly check per-instance CPU/GPU busy + network egress? If it's just cache pressure scaling won't help much.
Jordan T: metrics: canary pool cache hit dropped from 92% -> 37% at spike. CPU % steady. GPU util down slightly (waiting on KV). So likely cache key change causing high remote fetches -> tail latency.
Samir K: I'll prepare a rollback if we decide. deploy-bot: show last deployment?
deploy-bot: v5.3-canary deployed at 1947654200 by Jordan T. Canary weight: 15% (traffic-shift policy).
Alex R: immediate action: reduce canary weight to 3% to limit impact while we investigate. I'll run the traffic command.
Alex R: run: ```
# reduce canary to 3%
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.prod/v1/rollouts/traffic \
  -d '{"deployment":"v5.3-canary","weight":0.03}'
```
deploy-bot: success — canary weight set to 3% at 1947654335 (response 200).
Maya S: after weight drop p95 down to 220ms, p99 trending down to ~1.1s. Streaming errors reduced but still seeing occasional stalls.
Jordan T: collecting heap/trace from a canary instance for offline replay. Uploading to /internal/traces/1947654321-canary.tar.gz
Samir K: I recommend rollback if p99 doesn't stabilize under 800ms in 5m. Preparing rollback steps now.
Lia P: CS-ops: notifying impacted customers that we throttled canary and are prepared to roll back. Ticket updated: INC-19476.
Alex R: 2m after throttle: p95 ~180ms p99 ~600-700ms. Good trend. Can we confirm streaming chunking/resume behavior?
Jordan T: logs show streaming backpressure counters decreasing. Looks like clients that experienced stalls recovered when routed to stable.
Maya S: I'll leave monitoring on aggressive alerts for next 30m. If p99 climbs >900ms we rollback.
Samir K: rollback command ready: ```
# rollback canary -> v5.2
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.prod/v1/deployments/rollback \
  -d '{"deployment":"v5.3-canary","target":"v5.2"}'
```
Alex R: good. I'll hand off to Jordan in 25m for longer-term root cause and postmortem. Jordan, you're on deck for root cause and coord with model infra to revert kv_prefix_harmonize if needed.
Jordan T: on it. I'll also run localized replay against v5.3 with synthetic prefixes to measure impact and validate fix.
Lia P: CS-ops: will keep customers updated. Notifying enterprise accounts about potential token loss with webhooks.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call escalation rule triggered: if p99 > 900ms for >5m escalate to SEV oncall. Threshold query active.
Alex R: adding timeline to INC-19476 and start drafting mitigation blurb for slack and status page.
Maya S: handoff: Jordan T takes primary for RCA, Samir K standby for rollback exec, Lia P continues customer comms. I'll keep monitoring until 1950 UTC.
Jordan T: acknowledged. Will post a preliminary RCA and candidate fix by EOD.
CS-ops: thanks team. No refunds requested yet; customers appreciative of proactive notes.
Samir K: if rollback needed I'll execute after your go, Jordan.
Alex R: closing live paging sequence for now — mitigations effective, watch window open 30m. tagging follow-ups for postmortem: - verify kv key compatibility tests in CI - add canary traffic auto-slowdown rule on cache-hit drop - add streaming stall synthetic checks.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: INC-19476 updated: status -> mitigation, priority -> P2. Next update scheduled at 1947654588."
